StremIOS playback dependency: MobileVLCKit 3.7.4

This directory contains provenance, verified source-fetch and packaging recipes,
component manifests, replacement instructions and the unchanged LGPL 2.1
license. It contains no compiled framework. The app dynamically links VideoLAN's
official framework when building the VLC-enabled version; the selected source is
probed only after the user chooses Play. HLS uses AVPlayer; other supported containers use VideoLAN.

Prepare the official arm64 iOS framework from the project directory:

  python3 Vendor/MobileVLCKit/fetch-vlckit.py --sources

The default cache is .cache/vlckit inside the project checkout and is ignored
by Git. To use a different local cache:

  python3 Vendor/MobileVLCKit/fetch-vlckit.py --cache /absolute/cache --sources

The first run downloads the 232,899,504-byte official archive, verifies SHA256
BEFORE extraction, extracts only the iOS device framework, and selects its arm64
slice. A different preexisting archive/framework is rejected, not overwritten.
No simulator slices or dSYMs are extracted. No downloaded code is executed.
The helper requires Python 3.9+ and Apple's xcrun/lipo. It does not install an app,
accept a license, change Xcode selection, or run a device test.

Build with the existing scripts (Xcode must already be installed):

  DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  MS_VLCKIT_FRAMEWORK=/absolute/cache/arm64/MobileVLCKit.framework \
  ./scripts/build.sh /absolute/build-output

MS_VLCKIT_FRAMEWORK must identify the framework directory, not its parent.
Omitting it selects the project-local .cache/vlckit cache. The build's embed-vlckit.sh
checks the exact original arm64 binary hash, embeds the executable and Info.plist,
then ad-hoc signs the embedded framework before the app. Headers stay build-only.
The dependency's MinimumOSVersion is 9.0, its recorded build SDK is 15.4, and the
app still targets arm64 iOS 12.0. These metadata checks alone do not prove playback
or battery performance; actual-device tests are separate.

Link inputs:
  -F <framework-parent> -framework MobileVLCKit
  -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/Frameworks

The official podspec lists QuartzCore, CoreText, AVFoundation, Security,
CFNetwork, AudioToolbox, OpenGLES, CoreGraphics, VideoToolbox and CoreMedia;
libraries c++, xml2, z, bz2 and iconv. The prebuilt dynamic library records its
system dependencies. No second bundled third-party dynamic library is needed.
The original thin arm64 binary is 38,619,688 bytes. A compressed runtime archive
estimate was about 16 MiB; installed app size and playback memory are different
measurements. The preparation helper does not strip the verified binary.

Binary and source pinning

The authoritative VideoLAN release commit publishes the exact archive and hash:
https://github.com/videolan/vlckit/blob/b2edca9ca041eafad1408ee91a55e6d87f7e23d5/Packaging/podspecs/MobileVLCKit.podspec

Binary archive:
https://download.videolan.org/pub/cocoapods/prod/MobileVLCKit-3.0-20260922-1512.tar.xz
SHA256 c649c4c47bd065b3a5511746361b5a9066a34033f2df9cbc9454409c0f363b52

VLCKit source commit:
2c06f8f64ce6e8f48fd25337079a6051e0ca9bdd
https://github.com/videolan/vlckit/tree/2c06f8f64ce6e8f48fd25337079a6051e0ca9bdd

VLC base source commit selected by that build script:
6de05adcbaf2e8b85fe86aad4169393098628119
https://github.com/videolan/vlc/tree/6de05adcbaf2e8b85fe86aad4169393098628119

Apply all 42 patches from the pinned VLCKit libvlc/patches directory in lexical
order. They are part of this source recipe, not StremIOS modifications. The
official buildMobileVLCKit.sh performs the checkout and git-am steps. The pinned
.gitlab-ci.yml uses buildMobileVLCKit.sh -vf3 and
Packaging/create-distributable-package.sh -vm for the device/simulator archive.
Use the script's help and documented tool requirements before rebuilding; its
contrib recipes download additional source archives with recorded checksums.
The original CI used a Monterey/Xcode environment; rebuilding with a different
SDK/toolchain is not claimed to produce identical bytes.

The timestamped binary follows the September 22 source update; the intervening
September 30 commits change TV-only CI and package-release metadata. All 23
matching shipped public headers are byte-identical to this VLCKit commit. Binary
inspection reports libVLC "3.0.24 Vetinari" and changeset
"3.0.24-42-gcdceca9c6f", consistent with the pinned VLC base and 42 patches.
The last hash is a generated patched build commit, not an upstream VLC tag.
No independent byte-for-byte rebuild is claimed.

The fetch-vlckit.py --sources option downloads and verifies both immutable source archives.
Their URLs, lengths and SHA256 values are recorded in provenance.json. They
include the wrapper, VLC code, patches, build scripts and contrib recipes.
Contrib dependency archives are fetched separately by fetch-contrib-sources.py.
Do not describe the two archives alone as a complete dependency source bundle.

Preparing a public binary release

From the project root, fetch the checksum-pinned contrib inputs and assemble the
source/notices assets into a fresh output directory:

  python3 Vendor/MobileVLCKit/fetch-contrib-sources.py
  python3 Vendor/MobileVLCKit/assemble-source-bundle.py \
    --contrib-cache .cache/vlckit/contrib-sources \
    --upstream-cache .cache/vlckit \
    --output /absolute/fresh/release-output

The packaging recipe verifies every original archive, retains all 42 upstream
patches and 48 selected contrib source packages, and includes nested component
notices. The libmysofa archive is explicitly repacked to omit uncompiled acoustic
test datasets and Windows prebuilt files; library source and installed data are
unchanged. Original and distributed checksums plus the exact omission list are
included. Binary evidence identifies 45 packages; three additional build inputs
are supplied conservatively. See contrib-sources.json, binary-component-evidence.json
and SOURCE-AND-RELINKING.txt for the evidence and limits.

Publish the resulting playback-sources.tar.xz, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt and
SOURCE-AND-RELINKING.txt beside the matching application source and binary. Install
the generated notices as Resources/ThirdPartyNotices.txt before the release build
so a standalone IPA retains its notices. The assembler recognizes its previous
output when regenerating notices and does not recursively duplicate it.

The bundled prepare-bundled-sources.py validates every bundled file, extracts the
two upstream trees, applies the 42 patches and seeds the 48 source tarballs without
network access. This preparation was checked locally; a full framework rebuild
and byte-identical reproduction are not claimed. Upstream build tools and Apple
SDKs remain separate prerequisites. The instructions describe library replacement
and signing a modified app for the recipient's device.

License / modification / redistribution

Copyright belongs to VideoLAN and the respective VLCKit/libVLC contributors.
VLCKit and libVLC are supplied under LGPL version 2.1 or, where stated in the
source, later versions. See COPYING.LGPL-2.1.txt and the upstream source notices;
individual bundled dependencies retain their own licenses. The official script
configures a non-GPL contribution build. StremIOS does not modify VLCKit code;
it extracts an existing architecture slice and signs it for this installation.

Keep the upstream notices/license and source references with any redistributed
build. Preserve recipients' LGPL rights, including modifying/replacing the
library and reverse-engineering for debugging those changes. Dynamic linking
does not remove the corresponding-source and other license obligations. Before
public binary redistribution, provide the applicable corresponding sources,
including required patches, dependency source material and build information.
The source bundle and build scripts allow rebuilding the application; replacing
the library also requires intentionally updating the local integrity pin and
signing the modified app for the recipient's device. The default build rejects
an unreviewed or accidentally changed dependency.

The complete unchanged LGPL text, component notices and source references are
also included in the app's ThirdPartyNotices.txt. These scripts prepare local
artifacts; they do not publish a release or submit an app to a store. Keep the
matching source and notices assets available with binary downloads. Store terms,
Apple signing and platform eligibility are separate from source preparation.
